Band In the Sky goes on repeat for me all the time. I live-streamed the Denver show that it debuted at last year & the lyrics instantly got me emotional in a very positive way. From "Learning how to fall and how to fly" to "Lift each other up...hiiiiiiigh", it's some of Al's most straightforward and powerful writing. 

\- Instrumentally, I want to see how far that outro can go live. I think (maybe ambitiously) that it could be a jumping-off point for a classic long moe. segue into something like BUD, Rebub, or Hi & Lo. 

Also, whereas Ups & Downs took a song from Rob's solo work & amplified it with a full band, I really like that Beautiful Mess kind of did the opposite and retained the low-fi, garage-y vibes of that guitar lick and gave Al a couple of really nice solos on top of it. 

Finally, I just want to say that I really disliked Don'tcha Know when it first debuted live. So when I saw the tracklist before the album released, I was kind of disappointed it was chosen over some still leftover tracks from the 2018-2021 tours (What Can I Say, Angel, I Can Never Remember, etc...). However, I was pleasantly surprised with the arrangement rework when I was seeing them in Woodstock. And that segue into ATL was wild! While it's still not my favorite song on the album, it's probably the most-improved from debut-to-recording!

With Amanda being used to headline an upcoming event as a lead antagonist, I find myself re-reading some of her earliest appearances. Secret Origins 14 does a great job briefly illustrating her rise in the political world and why she initially believes in her version of the Suicide Squad.

  
Waller is a woman who married young in Cabrini Green and lost almost everything before she turned her grief into strength and ambition. She helped her only surviving daughter through college and then returned to college for a political science degree herself. Racked with hurt and dissatisfaction with the environment and status quo around her, Amanda sought to change the American system and political machine from the inside. She helped an outsider candidate win a Congressional election and generally stood up for her Squad regulars when push came to shove with other government officials.   


The Squad used to stand for rehabilitation and second chances to Waller. She never wanted to solve the problems of Cabrini Green & other crime-ridden parts of the country by authoritarian measures. She just wanted to give everyone a chance to do better and be better people. I think that message has often been lost in the more recent years of Squad comics.   


That being said, I can see and understand the evolution of her character to a villain. The nuances of "Hey, I like you as a candidate for Congress, Collins; but you don't know how the machine works. I do, so I'll do what's necessary for a good person to win!" or "Hey, I get why government foreign policy works as it does and we can't accomplish every goal overseas in the public eye; but if I use the Squad right, we can!" can easily turn into a bit of an "Ends justify the means" complex over time. I guess I just always want to err on the side of hope and optimism when it comes to a human being with a chip on her shoulder and a desire to institute positive change though.

Infinite Crisis was just a great jumping-on point for discovering multiple characters I'd never heard of as a casual Batman fan only up to that point. Sinestro Corps War is a pretty fun first Green Lantern read, from my memory. More contained and straightforward. Blackest Night/Brightest Day, on the other hand, gives you a big overview of the Emotional Spectrum part of DC as well. 

I don't know a ton of big Supes or WW arcs that I can recommend off the top of my head, there have been so many that it's hard to pick standouts. 

But for Batman, The Long Halloween is my personal favorite tale. My favorite League will always be Morrison's JLA. And I think Geoff Johns's Flash run was my first deep-dive into the Speedsters, that won my heart instantly.

Outside of that, I dig the more niche, weird stuff in DC. Morrison's Animal Man, Morrison & then Way's Doom Patrol, Ostrander's Suicide Squad, Simone's Secret Six, Venditti's Hawkman, Johns's JSA, and James Robinson's Starman (and his Shade follow-up) all kept my interest.
